clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says to check what's hiding behind the words 'vitamin C' on your label.

His story: sailors used to get scurvy on long voyages, until their navy found that citrus fruit - lemons, limes, oranges - stopped it completely.

The catch Kevin points to: most labels list 'vitamin C' as ascorbic acid. Give someone with scurvy plain ascorbic acid today, he says, and it doesn't work the way citrus does. In nature, vitamin C always travels with bioflavonoids and other cofactors.

Next time you shop, look past the words 'vitamin C' and check what's actually attached to it.
